changes.before: Change badges.insert(3) to badges.insert(2). What prints before the iteration line?
changes.after: Keep one copy of each distinct value in a set.

before: A std::set<T> stores distinct keys in comparator order. With the default integer comparison, {3,1,3} contains only 1 and 3. It does not remember a count of repeated 3 values.
insert(value) returns a pair: first identifies the existing or added element, and second is true only when a new element was inserted. Duplicate insertion leaves the size unchanged.
The set’s values are its keys. Changing a stored value directly would break ordering; erase the old value and insert a new value instead.

Expected output or behavior: 0 2
1 3 . Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Insert a duplicate and a new badge; compare each success flag with the size change. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::set stores distinct values in comparison order. With ordinary integers, repeated equal values count as one item. It does not keep a count of how many duplicates were supplied.
insert tries to add a value. If an equal value is already present, the set keeps its existing item and its size stays the same.
insert returns a pair of results. first is an iterator to the stored item. second is true only when a new item was added.
The program prints 0 2, then 1 3 on the next line, with a space after each listed item. The repeated three is stored once, and inserting it again adds nothing.
The stored values also determine the set's order, so you cannot change one directly through its iterator. To replace a value, erase the old one and insert the new one.

before.question: Change badges.insert(3) to badges.insert(2). What prints before the iteration line?
before.explanation: 2 was absent, so insertion succeeds and raises the number of distinct keys from two to three.

after.question: Change badges.insert(3) to badges.insert(2). What does the first line print?
after.explanation: Two was absent, so it is added. The success result is true, printed as one, and the set now has three distinct values.
